summary_en: This study tests giving donor lymphocytes (white blood cells from the transplant donor) early after an allogeneic blood or bone marrow transplant in people with high-risk hematologic malignancies. Donor lymphocyte infusion is given on day +7 after transplant (or day +21 for one dose level), at escalating doses, after chemotherapy drugs given IV and sirolimus and mycophenolate given by mouth or IV. The record lists the study as Phase 1/Phase 2 and does not state a main outcome measure, but its stated objective is to learn whether early donor lymphocytes help reduce the risk of relapse.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la infusión de linfocitos del donante (glóbulos blancos del donante del trasplante) poco después de un trasplante alogénico de células madre sanguíneas o de médula ósea en personas con neoplasias hematológicas de alto riesgo. La infusión se administra en el día +7 después del trasplante (o en el día +21 para un nivel de dosis), en dosis crecientes, junto con medicamentos de quimioterapia por vía intravenosa y sirolimus y micofenolato por vía oral o intravenosa. El registro indica que el estudio es de Fase 1/Fase 2 y no señala una medida de resultado principal, pero su objetivo declarado es saber si los linfocitos del donante administrados temprano ayudan a reducir el riesgo de recaída.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 65 with a listed high-risk blood cancer, such as AML, ALL, MDS, lymphoma, or multiple myeloma.
Disease that has not responded well to standard treatment or has a high risk of relapse, per the listed criteria.
At least one potentially suitable HLA-matched or HLA-haploidentical donor.
Related donor aged 12 or older who is suitable and willing to donate blood, bone marrow, and stool for research.
not_for: Prior myeloablative conditioning for an autologous or allogeneic transplant.
Currently receiving other investigational agents, or prior experimental therapy not finished at least 3 weeks before conditioning.
Active non-hematopoietic cancer that is metastatic, relapsed or refractory, or locally advanced and not curable (non-melanoma skin cancer excluded).
Uncontrolled intercurrent illness that the investigator judges unsafe for transplant.
